name: YouTube Transcript
one_liner: TranscriptAPI.com is a third-party REST API for fetching YouTube video transcripts, channel/video search, and playlist data.

evidence.quote: 100 free credits to try the API — no card required.
claude mcp add --transport http transcript-api https://transcriptapi.com/mcp
100 free credits to try the API — no card required.
REST API with HTTP endpoints (curl examples provided throughout documentation).
Get Transcripts, Search YouTube, Search Within Channels, Browse Channel Videos, Track New Uploads (RSS), Extract Playlist Videos, Resolve Channel Handles
Unauthenticated probe -> HTTP 401; WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; body: {"detail":"Not authenticated"}

notes: Vendor is transcriptapi.com (third-party service exposing YouTube transcripts, not a YouTube-owned product). Self-serve signup with 100 free credits, no card required; paid tiers start at $5/mo for 1,000 credits. REST API with bearer-token API key auth (confirmed by live 401 probe returning www-authenticate: Bearer). Vendor also hosts its own MCP endpoint at /mcp on the same domain (self-serve, streamable HTTP transport), which counts as official since it's first-party. Note: the site's /mcp path itself returned 401 to unauthenticated WebFetch (expected, since MCP requires a session), so MCP quote is taken from the homepage's install instructions rather than the MCP endpoint response. Some docs subpages (/docs/api, /billing) failed to yield extractable text via WebFetch within the 6-fetch budget; homepage content was sufficiently detailed to cover all required claims.
